name: Access violation
explanation: The game tried to use memory it doesn't own. This is usually a bug in the game or a mod, sometimes an overlay or an unstable overclock.
what_helps: Update the game, turn off mods and overlays, and undo any CPU, GPU or memory overclock.
notes: Most common code. The faulting module says more; check the module rows first.

name: Fatal error (fail fast)
explanation: The game found a serious error and ended itself on purpose.
what_helps: Update the game and your graphics driver, and turn off mods.
notes: STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN, also used by __fastfail and abort(); in ucrtbase.dll it's almost always abort().

name: Fatal error (fail fast)
explanation: The game found a serious error and ended itself on purpose.
what_helps: Update the game and your graphics driver, and turn off mods.
notes: STATUS_FAIL_FAST_EXCEPTION

name: Fatal app exit
explanation: The game found a serious error and ended itself on purpose.
what_helps: Update the game, and verify its files in its launcher.
notes: STATUS_FATAL_APP_EXIT (FatalAppExit, older abort())

name: Assertion failed
explanation: A check inside the game failed, so it stopped.
what_helps: Update the game, and verify its files in its launcher.
notes: STATUS_ASSERTION_FAILURE

name: Heap corruption
explanation: The game's memory got damaged. This is usually a bug in the game or a mod, sometimes an overlay, an antivirus or unstable memory.
what_helps: Update the game, turn off mods and overlays, and undo any memory overclock (XMP/EXPO).
notes: Often reported in ntdll.dll.

name: Stack overflow
explanation: The game ran out of its stack memory, usually because of a bug in the game or a mod.
what_helps: Update the game and turn off mods.

name: Out of memory
explanation: The PC ran out of memory while the game was running.
what_helps: Close other apps while playing, and let Windows manage the page file size.

name: Out of memory
explanation: Windows ran out of resources the game needed.
what_helps: Close other apps while playing, and let Windows manage the page file size.
notes: STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES

name: Page file too small
explanation: Windows ran out of virtual memory: the memory and the page file were full.
what_helps: In Advanced system settings › Performance › Virtual memory, let Windows manage the page file size, and keep some free space on the system drive.
notes: STATUS_COMMITMENT_LIMIT. Very common with large games on PCs with 16 GB or less and a fixed small page file.

name: Illegal instruction
explanation: The game used a processor instruction this PC's processor doesn't have, often AVX or AVX2.
what_helps: Check the game's minimum processor. If the PC meets it, undo any CPU overclock and update the BIOS.
notes: STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION. New games often need AVX2; can also be an unstable CPU.

name: Privileged instruction
explanation: The game used a processor instruction it isn't allowed to use, which usually means its code is damaged.
what_helps: Verify the game's files in its launcher, and undo any CPU overclock.

name: Divide by zero
explanation: The game divided a number by zero, a bug in the game or a mod.
what_helps: Update the game and turn off mods.

name: Number overflow
explanation: A number in the game got too large, a bug in the game or a mod.
what_helps: Update the game and turn off mods.

name: Divide by zero
explanation: The game divided a number by zero, a bug in the game or a mod.
what_helps: Update the game and turn off mods.
notes: STATUS_FLOAT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO

name: Invalid calculation
explanation: The game made a calculation that can't be done, a bug in the game or a mod.
what_helps: Update the game and turn off mods.
notes: STATUS_FLOAT_INVALID_OPERATION

name: Invalid handle
explanation: The game used something Windows had already closed, a bug in the game.
what_helps: Update the game.

name: Error during an error
explanation: The game hit a second error while handling the first one.
what_helps: Update the game and turn off mods.
notes: STATUS_NONCONTINUABLE_EXCEPTION

name: Unhandled error
explanation: The game hit an error it didn't handle.
what_helps: Update the game and turn off mods.
notes: STATUS_UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION

name: Error in a callback
explanation: An error happened while Windows was calling into the game, often caused by an overlay, a mod or a driver.
what_helps: Turn off overlays and mods, and update your graphics driver.
notes: STATUS_FATAL_USER_CALLBACK_EXCEPTION

name: Invalid runtime call
explanation: The game passed something invalid to the Visual C++ runtime, a bug in the game.
what_helps: Update the game, and repair the Visual C++ Redistributable.
notes: STATUS_INVALID_CRUNTIME_PARAMETER

name: Stuck (deadlock)
explanation: The game got stuck waiting for itself.
what_helps: Update the game and turn off mods.
notes: STATUS_POSSIBLE_DEADLOCK

name: Breakpoint
explanation: The game stopped at a debugging point, which usually means an internal check failed.
what_helps: Update the game, and verify its files in its launcher.
notes: STATUS_BREAKPOINT. Some anti-cheats also cause it when a debugger or a tool they don't allow is running.

name: Unhandled C++ error
explanation: The game hit an error it didn't handle.
what_helps: Update the game, and verify its files in its launcher.
notes: Microsoft C++ exception ('msc'); the event's module is usually KERNELBASE.dll.

name: .NET error
explanation: The game, which is built on .NET, hit an error it didn't handle.
what_helps: Update the game, and repair the .NET Framework in Windows Features.
notes: CLR exception ('CCR'); .NET Framework 4 and later. Details are in Windows' Application log, event 1026.

name: .NET error
explanation: The game, which is built on an older .NET, hit an error it didn't handle.
what_helps: Turn on .NET Framework 3.5 in Windows Features, and update the game.
notes: CLR exception ('COM'), .NET 2.0/3.5.

name: DLL not found
explanation: The game couldn't start because a file it needs (a DLL) is missing.
what_helps: Install the Visual C++ Redistributable and the DirectX End-User Runtime, then verify the game's files.
notes: Windows doesn't name the DLL. See the missing_dll rows: compare the game's imports with what's on the PC.

name: Wrong or damaged DLL
explanation: A file the game needs is damaged or is the 32-bit version where the 64-bit one is needed (or the reverse).
what_helps: Reinstall the Visual C++ Redistributable (x64 and x86) and the DirectX End-User Runtime, then verify the game's files.
notes: STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_FORMAT. Often a 32-bit DLL copied into System32 by hand.

name: DLL failed to start
explanation: A file the game needs couldn't start.
what_helps: Restart the PC, then reinstall the Visual C++ Redistributable and verify the game's files.
notes: STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED. Also happens when Windows is signing out or out of desktop heap.

name: Signing out
explanation: The game couldn't start because Windows was signing out.
what_helps: Start the game again.
notes: STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED_LOGOFF. Not a game problem; probably don't show a crash card.

name: Entry point not found
explanation: A file the game needs is too old for it.
what_helps: Install the latest Visual C++ Redistributable, update Windows and your graphics driver, then verify the game's files.
notes: STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND. Classic case: an old msvcp140.dll in the game's folder or System32.

name: Signature not valid
explanation: Windows couldn't verify the digital signature of a file the game loads.
what_helps: Verify the game's files in its launcher. If it continues, check Windows Security › Device security.
notes: STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_HASH. Seen with anti-cheat drivers and Memory integrity.

name: Access denied
explanation: Windows blocked the game from a file or folder it needs.
what_helps: If Controlled folder access is on in Windows Security, allow the game there. Antivirus apps can also block it.
notes: STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED. Controlled folder access blocking saves in Documents is a common cause.

name: Couldn't read from the drive
explanation: Windows couldn't read part of the game from its drive.
what_helps: Check that the drive is connected, then check it for errors and verify the game's files.
notes: STATUS_IN_PAGE_ERROR: a bad sector, a loose or sleeping external drive, or a network drive.

name: Drive error
explanation: The drive the game is on reported damaged data.
what_helps: Check the drive for errors, back up your files, and verify the game's files.
notes: STATUS_DEVICE_DATA_ERROR

name: Drive error
explanation: The drive the game is on stopped responding.
what_helps: Check the drive's cable or connection and check it for errors.
notes: STATUS_IO_DEVICE_ERROR

name: Damaged file
explanation: A file or folder the game uses is damaged.
what_helps: Check the drive for errors, then verify the game's files.
notes: STATUS_FILE_CORRUPT_ERROR

name: Drive full
explanation: The drive is full, so the game couldn't write what it needed.
what_helps: Free up space on the drive.
notes: STATUS_DISK_FULL. Binder's Free up space page fits here.

name: App error (Store app)
explanation: The game, an app from the Microsoft Store or the Xbox app, hit an error it didn't handle.
what_helps: Update the game and the Gaming Services app in the Microsoft Store, or repair the game in Settings › Apps.
notes: STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION

name: Closed
explanation: The game was closed from its console window.
notes: STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT; already treated as benign by CrashAnalysis.IsBenign.

name: GPU removed (DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED)
explanation: The graphics card stopped responding and Windows reset it.
what_helps: Update or reinstall your graphics driver, turn off any GPU overclock or undervolt, and check the card's power cables.

name: GPU hung (DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG)
explanation: The graphics card got stuck on the game's work and Windows reset it.
what_helps: Update your graphics driver, lower the graphics settings, and turn off any GPU overclock.

name: GPU reset (DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_RESET)
explanation: The graphics card was reset because of a problem in the game's commands.
what_helps: Update the game and your graphics driver.

name: Driver error (DXGI_ERROR_DRIVER_INTERNAL_ERROR)
explanation: The graphics driver hit an internal error.
what_helps: Update or reinstall your graphics driver.

name: Not supported (DXGI_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED)
explanation: The graphics card or its driver doesn't support something the game needs, often DirectX 12 or a newer feature level.
what_helps: Update your graphics driver and check the game's minimum graphics card. Some games have a DirectX 11 option.

name: Invalid call (DXGI_ERROR_INVALID_CALL)
explanation: The game made a graphics call the driver didn't accept.
what_helps: Update the game and your graphics driver.

name: Missing component (DXGI_ERROR_SDK_COMPONENT_MISSING)
explanation: A DirectX 12 file the game ships with is missing or doesn't match.
what_helps: Verify the game's files in its launcher, and update Windows.
notes: Agility SDK: D3D12Core.dll in the game's D3D12 folder.

name: Device lost (D3DERR_DEVICELOST)
explanation: The game lost the graphics card, often after switching windows, the display or the resolution.
what_helps: Play in borderless or windowed mode, and update your graphics driver.
notes: DirectX 9

name: Out of video memory (D3DERR_OUTOFVIDEOMEMORY)
explanation: The graphics card ran out of its own memory.
what_helps: Lower texture quality or resolution in the game.
notes: DirectX 9

name: Invalid call (D3DERR_INVALIDCALL)
explanation: The game made a graphics call the driver didn't accept.
what_helps: Update your graphics driver and the game.
notes: DirectX 9

name: Driver error (D3DERR_DRIVERINTERNALERROR)
explanation: The graphics driver hit an internal error.
what_helps: Update or reinstall your graphics driver.
notes: DirectX 9

name: Not available (D3DERR_NOTAVAILABLE)
explanation: The graphics card doesn't support a mode or setting the game asked for.
what_helps: Change the game's resolution or display mode in its settings file, and update your graphics driver.
notes: DirectX 9

name: Display driver stopped responding and recovered
explanation: The graphics card stopped responding and Windows reset it.
what_helps: Update or reinstall your graphics driver, turn off any GPU overclock or undervolt, and check the card's power cables.
notes: TDR; CrashAnalysis already reads it as driverReset.

name: Graphics card hang (VIDEO_ENGINE_TIMEOUT)
explanation: The graphics card stopped responding and Windows reset it.
what_helps: Update or reinstall your graphics driver, and turn off any GPU overclock or undervolt.
notes: Windows Error Reporting, Application log event 1001 with problem event name LiveKernelEvent and code 141.

name: Graphics driver timeout (VIDEO_TDR_TIMEOUT_DETECTED)
explanation: The graphics card stopped responding and Windows reset it.
what_helps: Update or reinstall your graphics driver, and turn off any GPU overclock or undervolt.

name: Stopped responding
explanation: The game stopped responding and was closed.
what_helps: Update the game and your graphics driver. If it was loading, give it more time before closing it.
notes: CrashRecord.Hang

name: Corrected hardware error
explanation: Windows recorded a hardware error, usually from an unstable processor or memory.
what_helps: Update the BIOS, and undo any CPU or memory overclock (XMP/EXPO).
notes: System log. Show only if logged during the session; whole-PC crashes are out of scope (§10).
